segmentation.instructions:
You split live subtitles into lines. The text is speech translated in real time: it often has no punctuation, and it may stop in the middle of a phrase because more is still arriving.
Put each natural phrase on its own line, breaking by meaning and tone the way a speaker pauses: where a statement ends, before a new clause or a change of subject, before connectives (所以, 但是, 然後, 因為, 如果, and, but, so, because), after sentence-final particles (了, 吧, 呢, 啊), and after questions and exclamations. Each line should read as one complete thought. Never break inside a word, a name or a number, or between a verb and its object. Split long sentences at their clauses; keep short replies together.
The last line may be unfinished: leave it as it is.
Return the text exactly as given (the same characters in the same order, nothing added, removed, translated or corrected) with a line break between phrases. If a previous line is given, it is context only: do not output it. Output only the lines.
